author: Han Li,Zhang Tong
description:
The US Department of Homeland Security (DHS) has said a Chinese PhD student at Princeton University in New Jersey, detained by immigration authorities last week, overstayed her authorised period of stay in the country in 2016.
A DHS spokesperson told the South China Morning Post on Monday that US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) carried out a “targeted immigration enforcement operation” at Ronald Reagan National Airport in Washington on November 19 to arrest Eva Yi Xie.
Xie was admitted...
title: US says detained Princeton PhD student from China overstayed visa in 2016

author: Finbarr Bermingham
description:
Amid heated superpower rivalry, a vast majority of Germans want to remain neutral between the United States and China, even as a major new survey also reveals anxiety about the economic threat posed by Beijing.
The Berlin Pulse, an annual survey, showed that 83 per cent do not want to pick a side between the world’s two foremost powers. Just two per cent wished to side with China, compared with 15 per cent for the US.
The desire for neutrality spanned party lines and demographics, and...
title: Germans reject choosing between US and China as faith in the West crumbles

author: Nayan Seth
description:
Jensen Huang’s dramatic return as Nvidia’s CEO on Monday, engineered through US President Donald Trump’s personal intervention, carries major implications for Washington’s AI policy, priorities within the administration and its rivalry with Beijing.
What began with US media reports of his alleged affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, quickly morphed into a wider saga involving spying allegations, suspected AI chip smuggling to China, tighter export controls...
title: Jensen Huang’s stunning return in 11 days – 5 key takeaways

author: Zhang Tong,Han Li
description:
As the United States and China compete for scientific leadership, Washington and a growing number of states are imposing restrictions on academic ties with China.
Since 2018, Congress and 23 states have introduced 158 bills curbing how US universities work with foreign scientists, students and institutions; 24 became law, according to a new tracker from the Committee of 100, a non-profit organisation of prominent Chinese Americans.
Its interactive map shows 13 states with a law or executive...
title: How US restrictions on China are reshaping the science race

author: Reuters
description:
Mexico and China agreed on Monday to create a working group focused on bilateral economic priorities, Mexico’s ⁠Economy Ministry said.
Economy ministers Marcelo ‌Ebrard of Mexico and Wang Wentao of China will look at ways to boost Mexican exports to China, the ministry said.
During talks in Beijing, Ebrard ⁠highlighted a persistent trade imbalance, noting that China ‌is set to export more than US$130 billion in goods to Mexico ‌this year, compared with roughly US$10 billion ⁠in ⁠Mexican...
title: Mexico and China agree to create working group to boost trade

author: Orange Wang
description:
China-US ties will remain broadly stable in 2027 despite “more confrontational dynamics” and rising tensions, a leading Beijing expert says.
Da Wei, director of Tsinghua University’s Centre for International Security and Strategy, said a core factor in sustaining the current stability was whether policymakers, particularly those in Washington, recognised the “mutual vulnerability” of the rival powers.
The shift in power on Capitol Hill was likely to strain the Trump administration’s ability to...
title: China-US ties to enter ‘more difficult’ 2027 but broad stability will hold: expert

author: Eve Qiao
description:
China’s most advanced destroyer, the Type 055, will be put on display for the first time at next month’s Zhuhai air show in an event with a growing emphasis on maritime power.
The PLA Navy said in a post on its social media account on Monday that it would bring operational equipment to the air show, which this year marks its 30th anniversary.
“Several types of in-service naval equipment will be shown to the public for the first time, offering a comprehensive look at the PLA Navy’s progress in...
title: China’s advanced Type 055 destroyer to make its Zhuhai air show debut

author: Ling Xin
description:
Chinese and American astronomers have found a planet nearly five times the mass of Jupiter circling a small, dim star, challenging the textbook view of how giant planets form and how many of them are out there.
The team, from Carnegie Science in Washington and Shanghai Jiao Tong and Tsinghua universities, spotted the planet – known as HIP 88962 b – with the Magellan Clay Telescope in Chile after 16 years of observations.
Its host star has only two-thirds the mass of our sun – too small to build...
title: Huge planet, tiny star: discovery challenges textbook view of how giants form

author: Gabriel Dominguez
description:
China’s J-35A stealth fighter could receive upgrades to its engines, weapons, electronic systems and radar evasion capabilities, according to a military commentator on state broadcaster CCTV, as Beijing continues to develop its newest land-based low-observable warplane.
Shao Yongling identified four possible improvements, including fitting the twin-engined jet with what she termed a “full version” of China’s WS-19 engine and widening the range of weapons carried internally, helping it to remain...
title: More power, more weapons: what’s next for China’s J-35A stealth fighter?

author: Laura Zhou
description:
An international court ruling of genocide against Myanmar might complicate Beijing’s diplomatic engagement with Naypyidaw and cast a shadow over Belt and Road Initiative infrastructure projects in the country, observers warn.
The landmark decision by the UN’s highest judicial body covers Myanmar’s 2017 military campaign against the majority-Muslim Rohingya minority in Rakhine state that killed at least 10,000 people and forced hundreds of thousands more to flee.
The decision handed down on...
title: How will China’s ties with Myanmar change with the ICJ’s genocide ruling?

author: William Zheng
description:
A Chinese ministry official has been sentenced to death for spying after being groomed and blackmailed into handing over dozens of state secrets to a foreign intelligence agency, according to a rare public disclosure by Beijing’s state secrecy apparatus.
The official, identified only by his surname, Ma, was convicted of espionage, stripped of his political rights for life and all his personal property was confiscated, according to an account published on Monday by Baomiguan, the official WeChat...
title: China sentences ministry official to death for leaking over 100 state secrets

author: Emiliano Martínez Viademonte
description:
China holds nearly 70 per cent of the world’s patents for turning farm waste into energy and useful by-products – a research stockpile born from domestic pressure to manage billions of tonnes of crop straw and manure.
Now Beijing is putting that intellectual property to work in Latin America. This year, a long-running partnership between China’s state biogas institute and Argentina’s national agricultural agency enters a new three-year phase, establishing a technology-transfer hub, developing...
title: China’s biogas tech turns Argentina’s farm waste into clean energy
